title: The Gaekwads of Baroda
subtitle: Marathas in Gujarat, and Sayajirao III's reforming state · 1721 – 1949
subject: baroda-state
intro: The Gaekwads began as commanders under the Dabhade Senapatis collecting tribute in Gujarat, and made Baroda (Vadodara) their capital. They allied with the British early, and as a princely state Baroda became known under Sayajirao III for compulsory education, social reform and patronage — including the scholarship that sent B. R. Ambedkar to Columbia.

events.title: A base at Songadh
events.summary: Pilaji Gaekwad, an officer of the Dabhade Senapati, fortifies Songadh and begins raiding and collecting tribute in Mughal Gujarat.

events.title: Defeat at Dabhoi
events.summary: Pilaji fights alongside Trimbakrao Dabhade against Peshwa Bajirao and is defeated; the Gaekwads come to terms with the Peshwa.

events.title: Pilaji assassinated
events.summary: Pilaji is murdered at Dakor by agents of the Mughal governor of Gujarat. His son Damaji succeeds.

events.title: Baroda taken
events.summary: The Gaekwads take Baroda from the Mughals; it becomes their capital.

events.title: Damaji submits to the Peshwa
events.summary: Damaji backs Tarabai against Peshwa Nanasaheb, is captured by treachery, and has to cede half his Gujarat revenues to the Peshwa.

events.title: Ahmedabad falls
events.summary: The Marathas take Ahmedabad, ending Mughal rule in Gujarat.

events.title: Panipat
events.summary: Damaji fights at Panipat and is one of the commanders who escape the disaster.

events.title: Alliance with the British
events.summary: Facing internal revolt, the Baroda government accepts British help and a subsidiary force — earlier than any other Maratha house.

events.title: Malharrao deposed; Sayajirao III chosen
events.summary: After being accused of trying to poison the British Resident, Malharrao is deposed. A 12-year-old boy from a distant branch of the family is adopted and becomes Sayajirao III.

events.title: Lakshmi Vilas Palace
events.summary: Sayajirao III completes the Lakshmi Vilas Palace in Baroda, one of the largest private residences ever built.

events.title: Free compulsory primary education
events.summary: Sayajirao III makes primary education free and compulsory throughout Baroda state — among the first such measures in India — and builds libraries, a university and modern administration.

events.title: Ambedkar's scholarship
events.summary: A Baroda state scholarship sends the young B. R. Ambedkar to study at Columbia University in New York.

events.title: Baroda merges into Bombay State
events.summary: Baroda state is merged into Bombay State; its territory is now in Gujarat.
